chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a Christian man who married a Christian woman, and she became a Muslim before he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The bond of marriage has been severed from him, and there is no dower for her, nor is there a waiting period upon her from him.'

key_terms.عِدَّةَ: Waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.عِصْمَتُهَا: The bond of marriage or hindrance preventing her from marrying others
key_terms.مَهْرَ: Dower or dowry given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Christian woman who converts to Islam before her husband sleeps with her?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'faskh' (automatic dissolution) in Shia jurisprudence, where the husband's religious status as a non-Muslim prevents him from maintaining the bond with a Muslim wife prior to consummation. Unlike cases where consummation has occurred, the absence of 'iddeh' and 'mahr' underscores that the marriage was valid but not fully perfected, reflecting the theological incompatibility between a Muslim woman and a non-Muslim man.
